summary: Recent discussions in the Spark community highlight a trial of an AI-powered code review bot using Claude on new pull requests, several SPIP proposals—including a language‑agnostic UDF protocol and a fixed‑dimension numeric VECTOR data type—and an issue with Istio’s strict mTLS mode affecting executor communication.

highlights.text: A trial of an AI‑powered code review bot using Claude is running on new Apache Spark pull requests, posting severity‑labeled comments without approving or LGTM.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] Automated AI code review on new Spark PRs (trial)

highlights.text: The SPIP proposal for a Language‑agnostic UDF Protocol aims to provide a unified API and execution protocol for user‑defined functions that can run outside the Spark engine via IPC.

sources.title: SPIP: Language-agnostic UDF Protocol for Spark

highlights.text: A SPIP proposal introduces a new Spark SQL data type for storing a fixed number of numeric values, adding a fixed‑dimension numeric VECTOR type to the logical type system.

sources.title: SPIP: Add a fixed-dimension numeric VECTOR data type

highlights.text: An issue with Istio’s STRICT mTLS mode rejecting traffic to pod IPs not backed by a Service is causing executor‑to‑executor communication failures in Spark, prompting a discussion on an opt‑in executor headless Service.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] SPARK-42411: Opt-in executor headless Service for Istio strict mTLS on K8s
